titulo: An afternoon doing what they do
subtitulo: Ask what's actually happening this weekend, instead of defaulting to the one attraction every guidebook already told you about
cena: Your guidebook has one plan for the afternoon. The person next to you, who actually lives here, has a completely different one, and it's better.
decisao: em que gastar a tarde livre — seguir o roteiro já pago do guia ou perguntar o que está realmente acontecendo e pedir para ir junto, que custa uma pergunta e muda o dia inteiro
frasePiso: The best afternoon plan is rarely in the guidebook. It's whatever's actually happening in the plaza this weekend.

steps.pt: One question opens a different kind of afternoon — not what should I see, but what's actually happening this week.

steps.es: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?
steps.pt: What are you doing this weekend?
steps.tts: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?

steps.pt: Turn the question back around — this gets you into someone's actual plan, not a tourist itinerary.

steps.promptPt: Ask what's happening in the plaza this weekend. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?
steps.pinyin: eye AHL-goh en lah PLAH-sah EHS-teh feen deh seh-MAH-nah
steps.pt: Is there anything happening in the plaza this weekend?
steps.tts: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?

steps.es: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.
steps.pt: Yes, there's a roving market on Sundays.
steps.tts: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.

steps.pt: A mercado sobre ruedas sets up for one day and moves on — a different rhythm from a fixed tourist market. Ask to go along.

steps.promptPt: Ask if you can come along with them. Speak now.

steps.es: Claro, nos vemos a las diez.
steps.pt: Of course, see you at ten.

steps.promptPt: They just made room for you in their own weekend. Thank them for the invitation. Speak now.
steps.pt: How cool, thanks for inviting me.
Once there, you're not performing tourism — just at the market with everyone else, using the same sentence anyone would.

aprofundar.titulo: Local rhythm beats the fixed attraction

secoes.titulo: A mercado sobre ruedas is temporary by design
secoes.corpo: These street markets appear on a fixed day of the week in a given neighbourhood and pack up afterward — very different from a permanent tourist market, and worth asking about specifically since the schedule varies by area.

secoes.titulo: The plaza is the default social space
secoes.corpo: In many Mexican towns and neighbourhoods, the central plaza is where weekend life actually happens — asking what's on there is a reliable way to find something real rather than staged.
¿Puedo ir con ustedes? turns a piece of information into an invitation. Most people are glad to have you along, especially once you've asked rather than just watched from a distance.

permissao: You are allowed to ask a near-stranger if you can tag along. ¿Puedo ir con ustedes? is a normal, welcome question here — it isn't intrusive, and most people are genuinely glad to show off their own city's actual weekend instead of the guidebook version.
espelho: Asking a local friend 'what are you up to this weekend, mind if I tag along?' is something most people would happily do in their own city too — the only difference here is doing it in a second language, not the social risk of asking at all.
